description.summary: what an app can say about its window beyond xdg-shell

protocol.description:
A window extension any client may bind. It carries what a desktop-class app says about its toplevel that xdg_toplevel cannot: which parts accept the first click while the window is inactive, whether the compositor draws the shadow and rounds the corners, a placement the person asked for through the app's own controls, the window's role, its accessibility root and whether its document has unsaved changes. In return the client learns the window's emphasis (key, main or inactive) and its current placement.
This protocol is a draft. Until it is declared stable, version 1 may change in place with every client and the server updated together. Version 2 adds, after everything older, the person's request that the whole app quit; the event it adds says `since="2"` and is sent only to a client that bound the manager at version 2 or later.

interface.name: quire_window_manager_v1

description.summary: extends xdg toplevels

interface.description:
The global a client binds to extend its toplevels. Advertised on every connection.
The manager is also where the app hears that the person asked it to quit (`quit`, version 2): a quit is about the whole app, not one window, and an app with no window still has this object. A client that wants to hear it keeps a manager bound at version 2 or later for as long as it runs; destroying the manager ends the listening, and the compositor then closes the app's windows one by one instead.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the toplevel already has a quire_window_v1 object

request.name: get_window

description.summary: extend a toplevel

request.description: Creates the extension object of an xdg_toplevel. A toplevel has at most one; asking for a second while the first exists raises `already_constructed`.

description.summary: destroy the manager

event.name: quit

description.summary: the person asked the app to quit

event.description:
The person asked the app to quit (Command-Q, the Quit item of its menu, or the shell asking for it): save or ask, then exit. This is macOS's applicationShouldTerminate. It is sent in place of asking each window to close, and it reaches an app with no window.
The app answers by acting, not by a reply: it exits, or it stays (a "Save changes?" sheet, or it declines). The compositor shows the app as quitting for a short grace and takes it for running again if it is still there after that. An app that does nothing is not stuck: the person can close its windows one by one, and Force Quit still ends it.
Sent to every manager of the connection bound at version 2 or later. A client bound at version 1 never receives it, and the compositor closes its windows one by one.

interface.name: quire_window_v1

description.summary: one toplevel's extension

interface.description: Requests marked double-buffered take effect on the toplevel's next wl_surface.commit. Destroying the xdg_toplevel first makes this object defunct: every request but `destroy` then raises `defunct_toplevel`.

entry.name: bad_role
entry.summary: a role a client may not ask for

enum.name: window_role

description.summary: what kind of window this is

enum.description: `dialog` and `shell` are known to the compositor from other protocols (xdg-dialog, quire_shell_v1); a client cannot ask for them here.

entry.name: document
entry.summary: an ordinary document or app window

entry.name: utility
entry.summary: a floating panel that serves a document window

entry.name: shell
entry.summary: a surface of the desktop shell

enum.name: tile_zone

description.summary: the region a tiled window fills

enum.description: The eight zones of an output's usable area. `place_target` carries the same values for the same zones.

enum.name: place_target

description.summary: where a window is asked to go

enum.description: A tile zone, or one of fill, centre and restore. The first eight values are `tile_zone`'s.

entry.name: fill
entry.summary: the whole usable area, still a window

entry.name: centre
entry.summary: centred on its output at its own size

entry.name: restore
entry.summary: the size and place before the last placement

enum.name: placement_mark

description.summary: the window's current placement

enum.description: What the window's zoom control shows as current.

entry.name: full_screen
entry.summary: full screen in its own Space

enum.name: emphasis

description.summary: how much the window stands out

enum.description: The key window takes keyboard input; the main window is the frontmost document window of the active app while a utility window or panel is key; every other window is inactive.

entry.name: main
entry.summary: the active app's main window, not key

description.summary: who draws the window's frame effects

entry.name: client
entry.summary: the client draws its own shadow and corners

entry.name: compositor_shadow
entry.summary: the compositor draws the shadow and clips the corners

description.summary: whether the window's document has unsaved changes

request.name: set_first_mouse

description.summary: where a click on an inactive window acts at once

request.description: Double-buffered. Inside `region` (surface-local) a click on the inactive window both activates it and reaches the client; elsewhere it only activates. Null clears the region.

request.name: set_frame

description.summary: who draws the shadow and the corner clip

request.description: Double-buffered. `corner_radius` is in logical pixels and is read only for `compositor_shadow`.

request.name: request_placement

description.summary: ask for a placement

request.description: Asks the compositor to place the window. `serial` is the serial of the input event that led to the request; without a recent one from this client's seat the request is ignored, so windows never move on their own.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: serial of the user's input event

description.summary: declare the window's role

request.name: set_a11y_root

description.summary: where the window's accessibility tree lives

request.description: The D-Bus name and object path of the window's root accessible object.

description.summary: whether the document has unsaved changes

request.name: destroy

description.summary: drop the extension

request.description: The compositor forgets every value set through this object.

event.name: emphasis

description.summary: the window's emphasis changed

event.description: Sent once after creation and on every change.

event.name: placement

description.summary: the window's placement changed

event.description: Sent once after creation and on every change.
